findings.claim: The x74 (keyword-lookup) and x87 (destructure) are not caused by repeat. They come from the 3-argument `+`. jolt's compiler ignores a var's :inline, and the committed codemod (HEAD 4ce56eb, /home/user/cohost-baseline, which the quick-run numbers match) did not apply it either. So `(+ acc (:a m) (:b m))` calls core.clj's variadic arity: a rest seq, then `reduce1`, then `chunked-seq?` once, which is a stock `instance?`. In the committed code each stock `instance?` builds and calls a fresh `.isInstance` dispatcher (finding 2). destructure pays that twice per element: once inside the `+` and once in the `(seq? map__N)` test that core.clj's map destructuring emits. map-lookup, reduce-range and equality pay it zero times per element. Inferred from the quick run (not measured part by part): destructure minus keyword-lookup = (619.7-376.89) ms / 100k = 2.43 µs per element. That is one extra `instance?` plus about 0.1 µs of frames (a stock seq? frame and two stock get to RT-get calls, at the 15-20 ns per frame seen on fn-call and map-lookup). So one committed-code `instance?` is about 2.3 µs, roughly 60% of keyword-lookup's 3.77 µs per element. The rest of the variadic `+` path is about 15 frames, roughly 0.3 µs. About 1.1 µs I cannot attribute by reading; GC and allocation are the candidates.

findings.claim: One committed-code stock `instance?` does five things, every call. (1) It calls `dot`. `dot` hashes the method-name string for its `record-members` test, then allocates a five-clause closure whose last clause is variadic. jolt registers every such closure, when it is created, in a weak eq-hashtable under a mutex. (2) Calling that closure runs `host-object?` on the class-token symbol, with no per-type cache. That goes through the adapter's `cap` (an atom deref and a map lookup) to jolt's `:user-type?`, which builds `(str (class x))` and makes two host string-method calls (.startsWith, .contains), each dispatched through jolt's chain of string=? tests. (3) `-isInstance` calls `instance-of?`. (4) `instance-of?` calls the unmemoized `canon`. Its `has-dot?` scans 'clojure.lang.IChunkedSeq' backwards one character at a time: 12 steps, each allocating a 1-char string via `(str (nth (name sym) i))`. (5) Then the interface-preds lookup, the predicate, and `builtin?`. How the inferred ~2.3 µs splits across these is an estimate from jolt's own per-op notes, not measured; probes P4-P6 measure each part.

findings.claim: repeat is not the cost. The per-element loop is jolt's own reduce on both sides. Stock repeat becomes cohost.shim/Repeat-create, which is jolt's own repeat, so both sides walk the same lazy sk-repeat cells. core/protocols.clj is never booted (policy skips its `load`), but stock reduce still reaches jolt's reduce. `(instance? clojure.lang.IReduceInit coll)` falls to the predicate's host fallback. jolt registers Repeat and LongRange as IReduce, which extends IReduceInit, so the test is true. `.reduce` then goes to `-reduce`, which is jolt's reduce. Had the test been false, `clojure.core.protocols/coll-reduce` is rewritten to cohost.shim/protocols-coll-reduce, also jolt's reduce. In jolt-reduce, iface-method is #f for any seq, and reduce-seq calls `(f acc x)` directly when f is a procedure. The stock side differs only once per reduce call.

It rewrites a literal-class instance? straight to cohost.shim/instance-of?, uses prebuilt dot$m dispatchers, memoizes canon, and caches host-object? per type with a :host-data? short-circuit. On jolt (:rewrite-inline? true) it also applies core.clj's :inline in the codemod and emits host aliases for shim statics that are host fns. So (+ acc (:a m) (:b m)) becomes (clojure.core/+ (clojure.core/+ acc (:a m)) (:b m)), and the destructure (get m :a) becomes jolt's own get. jolt evaluates def metadata, so the stock var's :inline is a real fn. target/bench-jolt.edn, written 10:53:57 ET with one timed call per side, shows: keyword-lookup 5.40 / 10.63 ms (x1.97); destructure 7.11 / 36.37 ms (x5.1); map-lookup 22.05 / 30.38 ms (but the host's first call took 10.47, so that pair is noisy); reduce-range 4.58 / 9.74 ms; equality 0.785 / 0.661 ms. fixes.change: Stop building a dispatcher on every call, and stop routing literal-class instance? tests through the stock instance?. Rewrite (instance? <class literal> x) to (cohost.shim/instance-of? 'C x). Build dot$m once per method and emit it. Memoize canon and test interface tokens first. Cache host-object? per type, with a :host-data? short-circuit. All of this is already in the working tree: rewrite.cljc:917-923 and 396-400, boot.cljc make-ctx install-dots!, shim.cljc:204-220 and 1836-1845, hosts/jolt.clj:61. Listed because it is the fix for the measured x74 and x87.
fixes.removes: Per stock instance? call, which happens once per element in keyword-lookup and twice in destructure: the closure allocation and jolt's mutex-guarded weak-table registration; the record-members string hash; user-type?'s (str (class x)) and two host string calls; canon's 12-step character loop with 1-char string allocations; and three var frames (instance?, the dispatcher, -isInstance).
fixes.risk: Low. Compiled call sites no longer see a with-redefs of instance?, which matches the JVM, where instance? is compiled as an intrinsic. The per-type host-object? cache assumes :user-type? depends only on the class; java.clj:84-94 reads only class-determined facts. The cache grows by one entry per class seen.

fixes.change: On jolt (:rewrite-inline? true), apply core.clj's :inline expansions in the codemod, and emit the host's own fn for a shim static whose value is that fn (Numbers-add becomes clojure.core/+, RT-get becomes clojure.core/get). Already in the working tree: rewrite.cljc inline-expansion (871-881, used at 962) and rw-static (363); boot.cljc host-aliases (92) and inline-fn (121).
fixes.removes: For (+ a b c): the variadic arity's rest seq, reduce1, and its seq/chunked-seq?/first/next frames, including the instance? inside them. For (get m k): two frames. The stock body becomes the same jolt natives the host compiles to (jolt-n+, jolt-get).
fixes.risk: Low to medium. An inlined arity no longer follows a redefinition of the stock var (with-redefs of + or get), which matches JVM Clojure. The inline fns run at rewrite time and read *unchecked-math* then, also as on the JVM. inline-fn does one ns-resolve per rewritten list form, so boot and compile time go up by an amount I have not measured. inline-expansion swallows expansion errors and falls back to a plain call, which can hide a broken :inline.

fixes.change: Proposed, for destructure's remaining x5: specialize class tests at rewrite time. For a literal token, emit a prebuilt per-token predicate cohost.shim/is$<token>, installed once like dot$m and closing over that token's interface pred and its host-instance? fallback. Add a small cohost table of :inline forms for core.clj's one-line class predicates (seq? becomes (cohost.shim/is$clojure.lang.ISeq ~x); likewise chunked-seq? and similar), so destructure's (seq? map__N) compiles to one call. Inside is$T, when the pred answers false, use one cheap adapter test for 'the host's own collection' before falling back to builtin?, whose coll? on jolt is a chain of three closures.
fixes.removes: Per element in destructure: the stock seq? frame, the instance-of? frame, the interface-preds HAMT lookup, and most of builtin?'s coll? chain. My estimate is about half of the measured 0.29 µs per element; unmeasured, see P3 and P9.
fixes.risk: Medium. is$T must keep the host-instance? fallback for deftypes and reifies that implement the interface; jolt answers coll?/seq? for jrecs implementing those interfaces (post-prelude.ss:281-295). The inline table means call sites no longer see a with-redefs of seq?. The extra adapter test must never classify a user type as host data.

fixes.change: Proposed, for reduce-range's x2.1: in cohost.shim/-reduce (shim.cljc:1570) and protocols-coll-reduce (shim.cljc:617), when f is identical? to the booted stock + (or *) root, pass the host's own fn (Numbers-add / Numbers-multiply, which are jolt-add / jolt-mul) to the host reduce, so jolt's open-coded (eq? f jolt-add) path in vec-reduce applies. This is equivalent: reduce calls f only with 0 or 2 arguments, and stock +'s 0-arity (0) and 2-arity (Numbers-add, now aliased to host +) are the host's.
fixes.removes: Per element: a call into the stock + closure plus jolt-add's rest list. The step becomes jolt-n+ open-coded inside vec-reduce-arith.
fixes.risk: Low. One identical? check per reduce call, against a lazily resolved cohost.core/+ root. A with-redefs of + changes the root, so the check fails and the original f is used, which is correct. It helps only + and * passed to reduce, not other stock fns passed as values.

fixes.change: Have bench record the source state it ran (git HEAD plus a hash of the loaded src files, or of the dirty diff) in target/bench-<label>.edn, and take at least 3-5 timed calls per side for the before/after tables, not one.
fixes.removes: No runtime cost; it removes measurement ambiguity. I could not tell which source state produced the 10:53:57 ET EDN. A single timed call on the allocation-heavy stock side can absorb a GC pause the host side never pays.
fixes.risk: None to runtime. Reading git from inside jolt needs a host capability, or a file the run script writes first.

probes.form: (let [v (vec (repeat 100000 {:a 1 :b 2}))] (time (reduce (fn [acc m] (+ acc (:a m) (:b m))) 0 v)) (time (reduce (fn [acc m] (+ acc (:a m) (:b m))) 0 (repeat 100000 {:a 1 :b 2}))))
probes.tests: That repeat is not the cost. Claim: the two times are within about 2x of each other on either tree; jolt reduces both natively (vec-reduce for the vector, reduce-seq for the repeat). Refuted if the repeat version is 5x or more slower than the vector version.

probes.form: (let [p +] (time (reduce (fn [acc m] (p acc (:a m) (:b m))) 0 (repeat 100000 {:a 1 :b 2}))) (time (reduce (fn [acc m] (p (p acc (:a m)) (:b m))) 0 (repeat 100000 {:a 1 :b 2}))))
probes.tests: That the 3-argument stock + carries keyword-lookup's cost. Calling + through the local p prevents the working tree's inline expansion (inline-expansion skips locals). Claim: the 3-argument form is 5x or more the nested 2-argument form. On the committed tree, roughly 350 ms versus 10-20 ms. Refuted if the two are within 2x.

probes.form: (do (time (reduce (fn [n m] (if (seq? m) n (inc n))) 0 (repeat 100000 {:a 1 :b 2}))) (time (reduce (fn [n m] (inc n)) 0 (repeat 100000 {:a 1 :b 2}))))
probes.tests: The cost of one stock seq?, that is one instance?, per element. Claim on the committed tree: about +230 ms per 100k (the ~2.3 µs inferred round trip). Claim on the working tree: about +25-30 ms (destructure's residual). Refuted if the committed-tree difference is under 50 ms (then instance? is not the dominant committed-code cost), or the working-tree difference is under 5 ms (then seq? is not destructure's residual).

The committed code's per-call cost of building a dispatcher, and how much of it is jolt's variadic-closure registration (mutex plus weak table). Valid on either tree, since dot still exists. Claim: the variadic closure costs at least 100 ns more per creation than the fixed-arity one, and the dot call costs at least as much as the variadic closure. Refuted if variadic and fixed-arity creation are within about 20 ns; then the round trip's cost sits in host-object? or canon (P5, P6).

instance-of? alone, including canon. Run once on each tree. Claim: the committed tree, with its unmemoized canon and 12-step has-dot? loop, is at least 0.4 µs per call slower than the working tree's memoized, token-first version. Refuted if the two trees are within 0.1 µs per call.

host-object? on a class-token symbol. Run once on each tree. Claim: committed tree (uncached; adapter :user-type? builds (str (class x)) and makes .startsWith/.contains host calls) is 0.3 µs or more per call; working tree (:host-data? is true for a symbol) is under 0.05 µs. Refuted if the committed tree is under 0.1 µs per call.

That reduce-range's x2.1 is the lost (eq? f jolt-add) fast path. Numbers-add is jolt's own + value (shim.cljc:521). Claim: the second form takes about the host time (about 4.6 ms) and the first about 9.7 ms. Refuted if both take about the same time.

Which branch stock reduce takes on jolt. Not timed. Claim: [true true true], so the .reduce branch runs, then -reduce, then jolt's reduce. A false answer means the protocols-coll-reduce branch, which also ends in jolt's reduce, so no performance conclusion changes.

probes.form: (do (time (reduce (fn [acc {:keys [a b]}] (+ acc a b)) 0 (repeat 100000 {:a 1 :b 2}))) (time (reduce (fn [acc m] (+ acc (get m :a) (get m :b))) 0 (repeat 100000 {:a 1 :b 2}))))
probes.tests: That destructure's working-tree residual is the seq? test and not the gets, which the working tree inlines to jolt-get. Claim: the destructuring form is about 25-30 ms slower per 100k. Refuted if the difference is under 5 ms.

probes.form: (do (time (reduce (fn [acc m] acc) 0 (repeat 100000 {:a 1 :b 2}))) (time (reduce (fn [acc m] (+ acc (:a m) (:b m))) 0 (repeat 100000 {:a 1 :b 2}))))
probes.tests: Where keyword-lookup's working-tree residual (x1.97, about 52 ns per element) lives. If the empty-body floor is already about 10 ms, the residual is in reaching or running jolt's reduce over a stock closure, not in the body. If the body adds 4 ms or more over the floor, the body is not compiling to jolt's natives; cross-check with P2's nested form.
